mainTopic: A גוי's wedding feast, the holiday of קרטסים, and the history of Roman rule, the סנהדרין, and סמיכה
overview: This amud finishes the rule about a גוי's wedding feast (הילולא). For 30 days after the wedding, every feast is forbidden. After that, until twelve months, a feast is forbidden only if he says it is for the wedding. The forbidden period begins when they start making beer for the wedding, and an אדם חשוב is stricter. Next the גמרא explains קרטסים, a Roman holiday marking the day רומי seized power. רב יוסף says רומי seized power twice. רב דימי then tells how רומי beat the Greeks by allying with ישראל, kept faith with ישראל for twenty-six years, and then turned on them. To prove those dates, the גמרא brings רבי יוסי's tradition about events before the חורבן, including the סנהדרין leaving its place forty years earlier. The גמרא concludes that this move ended דיני נפשות, not דיני קנסות, which רבי יהודה בן בבא kept alive by giving סמיכה at the cost of his life. The amud ends by starting a challenge to the 180-year figure, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The 30-day rule for a גוי's wedding feast
steps.stepSummary: For 30 days after the wedding, every feast is forbidden. After that, only a feast he says is for the wedding is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: During all thirty days, whether he told him it was because of the wedding or did not tell him, it is forbidden. From then on, if he told him it was because of the wedding, it is forbidden. If he did not tell him, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a rule about when a Jew may attend a feast made by a גוי around the time of his son's wedding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wedding feast counts like a festival, because the גוי thanks his idol for it. For the first 30 days, we assume every feast is part of the celebration. After 30 days we no longer assume that, so it depends on whether he says the feast is for the wedding.

keyTerms.meaning: From here on, after that point

phrases.english: During all thirty days,
phrases.notes: This is the end of a rule that began earlier, about a feast a גוי makes for his son's wedding. The thirty days count from the wedding.

phrases.english: whether he told him it is because of the wedding celebration

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵין לָא אָמַר לֵיהּ מֵחֲמַת הִלּוּלָא — אָסוּר,
phrases.english: or did not tell him it is because of the wedding celebration, it is forbidden.
From then on,

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמַר לֵיהּ מֵחֲמַת הִלּוּלָא — אָסוּר,
phrases.english: if he told him it is because of the wedding celebration, it is forbidden,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא אָמַר לֵיהּ מֵחֲמַת הִלּוּלָא — שְׁרֵי.
phrases.english: and if he did not tell him it is because of the wedding celebration, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּל תְּלָתִין יוֹמִין
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Within 30 days of the wedding, every feast is forbidden. After that, a feast is forbidden only if he says it is for the wedding.
steps.whatToRemember: First 30 days: always forbidden. After 30 days: forbidden only if he says it is for the הילולא.

steps.title: Until when does the wedding connection last?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how long a feast can still count as part of the wedding when he says it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when he tells him it is because of the wedding, until when is it forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for an end point to the second part of the rule. This question sets up רב פפא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule said that after 30 days, a feast is forbidden if he says it is for the wedding. That cannot go on forever, so the גמרא wants to know when the wedding stops counting.

phrases.english: And when he told him it is because of the wedding celebration,
until when is it forbidden?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי אָמַר לֵיהּ מֵחֲמַת הִלּוּלָא, עַד אֵימַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the time limit of the second half of step 1's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How long after the wedding a feast declared to be for the wedding stays forbidden.

steps.title: רב פפא: twelve months
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that the wedding connection lasts twelve months.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: until twelve months of the year.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives the end point: twelve months after the wedding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Within the first year, a feast he says is for the wedding is still treated as part of it. After twelve months, the link is considered over.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Until twelve months of the year.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: עַד תְּרֵיסַר יַרְחֵי שַׁתָּא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The prohibition lasts until twelve months after the wedding.

steps.title: When does the prohibition begin?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks from what point before the wedding the feasts become forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And at the beginning, from when is it forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know the end point, the גמרא asks about the starting point. This question sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wedding celebrations begin before the wedding day itself, so the גמרא wants to know how early the festival status starts.

keyTerms.meaning: At the beginning, at the start

phrases.english: And at the beginning, from when is it forbidden?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמֵעִיקָּרָא מֵאֵימַת אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the start point to match the end point given in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The starting point of the wedding festival period.

steps.title: From when they start preparing the barley
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא, quoting רבא, says it begins when they put barley into the mortars to make beer for the wedding.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said in the name of רבא: from when they put barley into the mortars.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the starting point: once the wedding preparations begin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting barley in the mortars was the first step in making beer for the wedding feast. Once preparations start, the celebration is already underway.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said in the name of Rava:
From when they put barley into the mortars.
phrases.notes: That's the barley being crushed to brew beer for the wedding, the very first step of getting ready.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is forbidden from when they begin preparing beer for the wedding.
steps.whatToRemember: The wedding festival period runs from the start of preparations until twelve months after the wedding.

steps.title: A story of a רב who refused after twelve months
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the twelve-month limit. רב יצחק בריה דרב משרשיא refused to eat at a גוי's feast even after twelve months.
steps.simpleTranslation: And after twelve months is it permitted? But רב יצחק the son of רב משרשיא came to the house of a certain גוי after twelve months, heard him giving thanks, and withdrew and did not eat!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רב פפא's twelve-month rule using a story about a רב who still held back after twelve months.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the prohibition ends after twelve months, why did רב יצחק refuse to eat? He heard the גוי thanking his idol, which shows the celebration was still connected to עבודה זרה.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, here is a case (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: And after twelve months of the year, is it permitted?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא
phrases.english: But Rav Yitzchak the son of Rav Mesharshiya
happened to come to the house of a certain gentile
after twelve months of the year,
and he heard him giving thanks,
phrases.notes: He heard the גוי thanking his idol for his son's wedding.

phrases.english: and he withdrew and did not eat!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְבָתַר תְּרֵיסַר יַרְחֵי שַׁתָּא שְׁרֵי? וְהָא
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's ruling that the prohibition ends after twelve months
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A רב acted as if it was still forbidden after twelve months, because the גוי was still thanking his idol.

steps.title: An important person is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב יצחק was an important person, so the case is an exception.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק the son of רב משרשיא is different, because he is an important person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the twelve-month rule by saying the story was a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An important guest makes the גוי rejoice more, so his visit could revive the celebration and the thanks to the idol. For an ordinary person, the rule of twelve months still holds.

phrases.aramaic: שָׁאנֵי רַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא,
phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak the son of Rav Mesharshiya is different,
because he is an important person.
phrases.notes: His visit made the גוי extra happy, which is why he thanked his idol even after the year.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי רַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the story is a special exception
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The story shows the prohibition lasts longer than twelve months for everyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: The twelve-month limit stands for regular people. An important person's visit is stricter.
steps.whatToRemember: Twelve months is the general rule. An אדם חשוב is stricter because his presence adds to the גוי's joy.

steps.title: What is קרטסים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next holiday listed in the משנה and asks what it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And קרטסים, etc.' What is קרטסים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new topic in the משנה and asks what the holiday called קרטסים is. This sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists festivals of the גוים, and קרטסים is an unfamiliar name. The גמרא wants to define it before going further.

phrases.english: The Mishnah taught: And Kratesis, etc.
What is Kratesis?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּקְרָטֵסִים וְכוּ׳. מַאי קְרָטֵסִים
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The definition of the holiday קרטסים.

steps.title: שמואל: the day Rome took power
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל, who says קרטסים is the day Rome seized power.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: the day on which Rome seized rule.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל defines קרטסים as the anniversary of Rome taking power.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this explanation, קרטסים is not a separate holiday. It is simply the name of the day Rome celebrated gaining its empire.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The day on which Rome seized rule.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: קרטסים is the day Rome seized power.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists them as two holidays
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל from a ברייתא that lists קרטסים and the day Rome took power separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: 'קרטסים, and the day on which Rome seized rule'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks שמואל's definition by quoting a ברייתא that names the two as different holidays.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If קרטסים is the day Rome took power, the ברייתא would not list them one after the other as two items. The list suggests they are separate days.

phrases.english: But it was taught in a baraita: Kratesis
and the day on which Rome seized rule!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: קְרָטֵסִים וְיוֹם שֶׁתָּפְסָה בּוֹ רוֹמִי מַלְכוּת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists the two as separate holidays, so they cannot be the same day.

steps.title: רב יוסף: Rome took power twice
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that Rome seized power on two occasions, so there are two separate celebrations.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Rome seized power twice. Once in the days of Queen Cleopatra, and once when it seized power in the days of the Greeks.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף resolves the contradiction by explaining that Rome had two separate conquests, each with its own holiday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both days celebrate Rome seizing power, so שמואל's definition is correct. The ברייתא lists two items because there were two separate conquests, one under קלפטרא and one in the time of the יונים.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Rome seized power two times,
one in the days of Queen Cleopatra,
and one that it seized in the days of the Greeks.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: שְׁתֵּי תְּפִיסוֹת תָּפְסָה רוֹמִי
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the case: two different events with similar descriptions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: There was only one day of Rome seizing power, so the ברייתא's two items contradict שמואל.
steps.terutzMaskana: Rome had two conquests. קרטסים is one, and the ברייתא's 'day Rome seized power' is the other.
steps.whatToRemember: Both holidays mark Rome seizing power, but on two separate occasions. That is why the ברייתא lists them separately.
steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף is not rejecting שמואל. He keeps שמואל's definition and explains why the ברייתא lists two days.

steps.title: Rome partners with Israel to defeat the Greeks
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports that the Romans fought thirty-two battles against the Greeks and could not win until they allied with ישראל, agreeing to share kingship and governorship.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came from ארץ ישראל, he said: The Romans fought thirty-two battles with the Greeks and could not beat them. Then they made ישראל their partners, with this deal: if the kings come from us, the governors come from you; if the kings come from you, the governors come from us.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story from רב דימי that fills in the background of one of the two times רומי took power, which רב יוסף mentioned in the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף said רומי seized power twice. This story describes one of those times: Rome only won against the Greeks after joining forces with ישראל. The deal promised ישראל a real share in ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: They made a deal, they set a condition
Governors, officials who rule under the king

phrases.english: As when Rav Dimi came, he said:
Thirty-two battles
the Romans waged with the Greeks,
and they could not defeat them,
until they made the Jewish people their partners,
and this is the condition they set with them:
If the kings are from us, the governors are from you;
if the kings are from you, the governors are from us.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּכִי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the historical background for one of the two times רומי took power, as רב יוסף said in Step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rome beat the Greeks only by allying with ישראל and promising to share rule with them.

steps.title: Rome proposes settling the dispute by judgment
steps.stepSummary: The Romans suggest replacing war with a ruling, and ask the Greeks whether a pearl or a precious stone should be the base for the other. The Greeks answer that the pearl is the base.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Romans sent a message to the Greeks: Until now we have fought with battles; now let us decide by judgment. A pearl and a precious stone: which one should be the base for the other? The Greeks answered: the pearl should be the base for the precious stone.
steps.whatsHappening: The Romans start a clever line of questions to get the Greeks to agree to a principle. This step sets up the next questions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the less important item serves as the setting for the more important one. The Greeks agree that the pearl serves the precious stone. Each answer will build toward a trap.

keyTerms.meaning: Judgment, a legal ruling instead of war
Base, the setting that holds something more important

phrases.english: And the Romans sent to the Greeks:
Until now we have acted through battle;
now let us act through judgment.
A pearl and a precious stone:
which of them should be made a base for the other?
They sent back to them: the pearl for the precious stone.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁלַחוּ לְהוּ רוֹמָאֵי לְיַוְנָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story: after forming the alliance, Rome challenges the Greeks with a ruling instead of a battle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Greeks agree that the lesser item serves as the base for the greater one, starting with pearl below precious stone.

steps.title: The chain of value rises up to the Torah scroll
steps.stepSummary: The Romans keep asking. The Greeks agree that a precious stone is the base for an onyx, and an onyx is the base for a ספר תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A precious stone and an onyx: which should be the base for the other? The precious stone for the onyx. An onyx and a ספר תורה: which should be the base for the other? The onyx for the ספר תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The Romans climb the ladder of value one step at a time, and the Greeks agree each time. This prepares the trap in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each answer puts the new item above the one before it. In the end the Greeks admit that the ספר תורה is above everything. That admission is exactly what the Romans need.

phrases.english: A precious stone and an onyx:
which of them should be made a base for the other?
The precious stone for the onyx.
An onyx and a Torah scroll:
which of them should be made a base for the other?
The onyx for the Torah scroll.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶבֶן טוֹבָה וְאִינָךְ, אֵיזוֹ מֵהֶן יֵעָשֶׂה בָּסִיס לַחֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same pattern of questions, raising the value up to the ספר תורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Greeks admit that the ספר תורה stands above all the precious items.

steps.title: Rome wins power, then turns on Israel
steps.stepSummary: The Romans spring the trap: they have the ספר תורה and ישראל on their side, so they should rule. They take power, stay loyal to ישראל for twenty-six years, and then subjugate them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Romans sent to them: If so, we have the ספר תורה with us and ישראל with us. They forced the Greeks to submit. For twenty-six years they kept their loyalty to ישראל; from then on they enslaved them.
steps.whatsHappening: The Romans use the Greeks' own answers to win, and the story ends by telling how Rome later broke its deal with ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the Greeks agreed that the ספר תורה is on top, the side holding it and allied with ישראל deserves to rule. That is how Rome took world power, which explains one of the two power seizures from Step 11. The partnership from Step 12 lasted only twenty-six years.
steps.whatToRemember: Rome rose to world power by allying with ישראל and claiming the ספר תורה was on its side. After twenty-six years it broke the deal and subjugated ישראל. This is one of the two times Rome seized power that רב יוסף mentioned.

phrases.english: They sent to them: If so,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in square brackets and some don't. They belong to the corrected wording.

phrases.english: we have the Torah scroll with us,
and the Jewish people are with us.
They forced them to submit.
For twenty-six years
they stood by their loyalty to the Jewish people;
from then on, they subjugated them.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַחוּ לְהוּ: אִם כֵּן אֲנַן סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה גַּבַּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the Greeks' admissions from Steps 13–14 to give Rome the victory, and closes the story begun in Step 12.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Rome gained world dominance by claiming the ספר תורה and ישראל were on its side, kept faith with ישראל for twenty-six years, and then subjugated them.

steps.title: Which verses did the Romans use, at first and later?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which פסוק the Romans used to explain their friendship with ישראל at first, and which one they used once they turned on them.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first, what did they expound, and in the end, what did they expound?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question about the story from step 15. It wants to know what פסוק the Romans pointed to at each stage, first when they were loyal and later when they took control.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 said the Romans stayed loyal for twenty-six years and then oppressed ישראל. This question assumes each stage had a 'reason' the Romans drew from the תורה. The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: They expounded, they read a meaning into a פסוק

phrases.english: At first, what did they expound,
phrases.notes: 'They' means the Romans from the story just told, during the friendly years.

phrases.english: and in the end, what did they expound?

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵעִיקָּרָא מַאי דְּרוּשׁ, וּלְבַסּוֹף מַאי דְּרוּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the scriptural basis behind the two stages of Roman behavior described in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק matched the Romans' early loyalty, and which matched their later oppression.

steps.title: From partners to masters: two verses about עשו and יעקב
steps.stepSummary: At first the Romans used עשו's offer to travel together as equals. Later they used יעקב's words calling עשו 'my lord' and himself 'his servant'.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first they expounded: 'Let us travel and go, and I will go alongside you.' In the end they expounded: 'Let my lord please pass ahead of his servant.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with two פסוקים from the meeting of יעקב and עשו. The first shows partnership, and the second shows one side ruling over the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רומי is linked with עשו. In the first פסוק עשו offers to travel as an equal, which matches the Romans sharing power with ישראל. In the second, יעקב calls עשו his master, which matches the later period when רומי ruled over ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: Alongside you, next to you as an equal

phrases.english: At first they expounded
"Let us travel and go, and I will go alongside you",
phrases.notes: בראשית 33:12. עשו is offering to travel next to יעקב, side by side as equals.

phrases.english: and in the end they expounded
"Let my lord please pass ahead of his servant".
phrases.notes: בראשית 33:14. Here יעקב speaks, calling עשו his master.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵעִיקָּרָא דְּרוּשׁ נִסְעָה וְנֵלֵכָה וְאֵלְכָה לְנֶגְדֶּךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Early on: נסעה ונלכה ואלכה לנגדך (equal partnership). Later: יעבר נא אדני לפני עבדו (mastery over ישראל).

steps.title: How do we know about the twenty-six loyal years?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source for the claim that the Romans stayed loyal to ישראל for exactly twenty-six years.
steps.simpleTranslation: The twenty-six years that they stood faithfully with ישראל, from where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the number twenty-six from step 15 and asks for proof of it. This sets up a teaching that will give us dates to work from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A specific number like twenty-six needs a basis. The גמרא is looking for a reliable historical tradition that fixes when Roman oppression began.

phrases.english: The twenty-six years
that they stood faithfully with ישראל
from where do we know?

steps.triggerLanguage: עֶשְׂרִין וְשֵׁית שְׁנִין דְּקָמוּ בְּהֵימָנוּתַיְיהוּ בַּהֲדֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מְנָא לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the number twenty-six stated in step 15 and asks for its source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing the Romans were loyal to ישראל for twenty-six years.

steps.title: The חכמים ask the sick רבי ישמעאל בר יוסי for his father's teachings
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא tells how, when רבי ישמעאל בר יוסי was ill, the חכמים asked him to repeat a few teachings he had said in his father's name.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב כהנא said: When רבי ישמעאל בר יוסי fell ill, they sent to him: 'רבי! Tell us two or three things that you told us in the name of your father.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins bringing its proof by telling the background story. This step only sets the scene; the actual teaching comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים wanted to make sure his father's teachings, from רבי יוסי, were not lost while he was ill. That shows the coming dates are a careful tradition passed from father to son.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of your father

phrases.english: As רב כהנא said:
When רבי ישמעאל בר יוסי fell ill,
they sent to him: Rebbi!
Tell us two or three things
that you told us in the name of your father.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא כְּשֶׁחָלָה רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בַּר יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces the source that will answer the question of step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setting the scene for a tradition of רבי יוסי passed on by his son.

steps.title: Three dates before the חורבן
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל בר יוסי gives three dates: Roman rule began 180 years before the חורבן, impurity was decreed on foreign lands and glass 80 years before, and the סנהדרין moved 40 years before.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: 180 years before the בית המקדש was destroyed, the wicked kingdom spread over ישראל. 80 years before the בית המקדש was destroyed, they decreed impurity on the land of the nations and on glass vessels. 40 years before the בית המקדש was destroyed, the סנהדרין was exiled and sat in the חנות.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the teaching the גמרא brings as its proof. The first date, when the 'wicked kingdom' took control, is the piece that matters for the twenty-six years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'wicked kingdom' (רומי) is said to have ruled over ישראל from 180 years before the חורבן. This marks when the oppression began, which is what the גמרא needs to work out the friendly period before it. The other two dates come along because they were part of the same tradition.

keyTerms.meaning: The land of the nations, land outside ארץ ישראל
The great court of seventy-one judges
Literally 'store', the name of the place the סנהדרין moved to

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think all three dates prove the twenty-six years. Only the first date, about Roman rule, is the proof. The other two dates are simply part of the same quoted teaching.

phrases.english: He said to them:
One hundred and eighty years
before the Temple was destroyed
the wicked kingdom spread out over ישראל,
phrases.notes: The 'wicked kingdom' is רומי; 'spread out' means it took control.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמוֹנִים שָׁנָה עַד לֹא חָרַב הַבַּיִת
phrases.english: eighty years before the Temple was destroyed
they decreed impurity on the land of the nations
and on glass vessels,

phrases.aramaic: אַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה עַד לֹא חָרַב הַבַּיִת
phrases.english: forty years before the Temple was destroyed
the סנהדרין was exiled
and sat in the חנות.
phrases.notes: The סנהדרין left its usual meeting place and moved to a spot called the חנות.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ מֵאָה וּשְׁמֹנִים שָׁנָה קוֹדֶם שֶׁנֶּחֱרַב הַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the content of the tradition introduced in step 19.
steps.raayaObject: The twenty-six loyal years of רומי (step 18).
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוסי's tradition that רומי's wicked rule over ישראל began 180 years before the חורבן.

steps.title: Why does it matter that the סנהדרין moved?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical הלכה follows from knowing that the סנהדרין moved forty years before the חורבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what הלכה is this relevant?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now looks at the third date from the teaching and asks why it matters in practice. This opens a side discussion about the סנהדרין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing where a court sat seems like plain history. The גמרא assumes it must teach something about הלכה, and asks what that is.

keyTerms.meaning: For what הלכה? What practical difference does it make?

phrases.english: For what הלכה is this relevant?
phrases.notes: This is asking about the last date: the סנהדרין moving to the חנות.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאי הִלְכְתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the third date from step 20 and asks for its practical meaning.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical הלכה results from the סנהדרין leaving its place forty years before the חורבן.

steps.title: They stopped judging דיני קנסות
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בר אבדימי says the point is that once the סנהדרין moved, they no longer judged דיני קנסות (cases of fines).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר אבדימי said: To teach that they no longer judged דיני קנסות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק בר אבדימי gives the practical result: after the move, דיני קנסות were no longer judged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The move is not just history. It changed what kinds of cases could be judged, and דיני קנסות stopped.

keyTerms.meaning: Cases of fines set by the תורה, such as paying double

phrases.english: רבי יצחק בר אבדימי said:
To teach that they did not judge cases of fines.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר אַבְדִּימִי לוֹמַר שֶׁלֹּא דָּנוּ דִּינֵי קְנָסוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: After the סנהדרין moved, דיני קנסות were no longer judged.

steps.title: But רבי יהודה בן בבא kept דיני קנסות alive
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: how can you say דיני קנסות stopped? רב praised רבי יהודה בן בבא because without him דיני קנסות would have been forgotten.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you really think they stopped judging דיני קנסות? But רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Truly, that man is remembered for good, and רבי יהודה בן בבא is his name, for if not for him, דיני קנסות would have been forgotten from ישראל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 22 using a statement of רב. רב praises רבי יהודה בן בבא for saving דיני קנסות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If דיני קנסות stopped forty years before the חורבן, there would be nothing left for רבי יהודה בן בבא to save later. רב's praise implies that דיני קנסות were still being handled after the סנהדרין moved, which seems to contradict step 22.

keyTerms.meaning: Does it enter your mind? Do you really think so?

phrases.english: Cases of fines, does that enter your mind?
But didn't רב יהודה say in the name of רב:
Truly, that man is remembered for good,
and רבי יהודה בן בבא is his name,
for if not for him
cases of fines would have been forgotten from ישראל!

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּינֵי קְנָסוֹת סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ וְהָאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק בר אבדימי's claim that דיני קנסות stopped once the סנהדרין moved.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב praises רבי יהודה בן בבא for preserving דיני קנסות, which implies they were still being judged after the move.

steps.title: Why would they be forgotten? Just learn them!
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רב's own wording: how could דיני קנסות be forgotten? People could simply study them.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Would have been forgotten'? Let them study them!
steps.whatsHappening: Before answering the challenge, the גמרא stops to question the wording of רב's statement. Laws you can learn from a book do not just disappear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if courts could not judge דיני קנסות, the חכמים could still learn those laws. So the word 'forgotten' seems too strong, and the גמרא wants to know what רב really meant. The answer comes next.

phrases.english: "Would have been forgotten"? Let them study them!

steps.triggerLanguage: נִשְׁתַּכְּחוּ לִגְרְסִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the statement quoted in step 23, before the main challenge is resolved.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word 'נשתכחו' in רב's praise of רבי יהודה בן בבא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Laws can always be studied even if not practiced, so they could not truly be forgotten.

steps.title: רב meant that fines would have stopped being judged, because Rome banned ordination
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רב's word 'forgotten' really means that דיני קנסות would have stopped being practiced, because Rome decreed death on anyone involved in סמיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב meant that the laws of fines would have stopped in Israel. The wicked Roman kingdom made a decree against the Jews: anyone who gives סמיכה will be killed, anyone who receives it will be killed, the city where it happens will be destroyed, and the area around it will be uprooted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 24: רב did not mean people would forget how to learn these laws. He meant that no one would be left who was allowed to judge them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only judges with real סמיכה can judge דיני קנסות. If the chain of סמיכה breaks, these cases can no longer be judged, even if everyone still knows the laws. Rome understood this and tried to break the chain by threatening death and destruction.

keyTerms.meaning: stopped, ceased to be in force
formal rabbinic ordination passed from teacher to student, needed to judge certain cases
the boundary area around a city

steps.confusionAlert: 'Forgotten' here does not mean people would forget the information. It means the laws would stop being put into practice, because there would be no ordained judges to rule on them.

phrases.english: Rather, the laws of fines would have ceased from Israel,
for the wicked kingdom decreed
religious persecution against Israel:
anyone who ordains will be killed,
and anyone who is ordained will be killed,
and a city in which they ordain will be destroyed,
and the boundary area in which they ordain will be uprooted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בָּטְלוּ דִּינֵי קְנָסוֹת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording question of Step 24 by reinterpreting 'forgotten' as 'ceased'.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב seemed to say the laws themselves would be forgotten, which makes no sense since they can be studied.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב meant the laws would stop being applied, because the chain of סמיכה would be broken by the Roman decree.

steps.title: רבי יהודה בן בבא secretly ordains five or six sages
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בן בבא went to an empty spot between two cities and their שבת boundaries and gave סמיכה to רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי, רבי שמעון, and רבי אלעזר בן שמוע; רב אויא adds רבי נחמיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did רבי יהודה בן בבא do? He went and sat between two big mountains, between two big cities, between two שבת boundaries, between אושא and שפרעם, and there he ordained five elders: רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי, רבי שמעון, and רבי אלעזר בן שמוע. רב אויא adds: also רבי נחמיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells the story behind רב's praise: how רבי יהודה בן בבא kept סמיכה alive despite the Roman decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He picked a place that did not belong to any city or city boundary, so the decree to destroy a city or uproot a boundary could not hurt anyone else. By ordaining these students, he made sure ordained judges would continue, so דיני קנסות could still be judged.

keyTerms.meaning: the boundary areas around cities beyond which one may not walk on שבת

steps.whyThisMatters: These are the great תנאים of the next generation, whose teachings fill the משנה. Their ordination shows that ordained judges continued for many years after the חורבן.

phrases.aramaic: מָה עָשָׂה רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בָּבָא?
phrases.english: What did Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava do?

phrases.aramaic: הָלַךְ וְיָשַׁב בֵּין שְׁנֵי הָרִים גְּדוֹלִים,
phrases.english: He went and sat between two large mountains,
and between two large cities,
between two Shabbat boundaries,
between Usha and Shefaram,
and there he ordained five elders:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir, and Rabbi Yehuda, and Rabbi Yosei,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן שַׁמּוּעַ,
phrases.english: and Rabbi Shimon, and Rabbi Elazar ben Shammua,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב אַוְיָא מוֹסִיף: אַף רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה.
phrases.english: and Rav Avya adds: also Rabbi Neḥemya.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה עָשָׂה רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בָּבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the explanation by telling how רבי יהודה בן בבא got around the Roman decree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה בן בבא kept the chain of סמיכה alive by ordaining five or six sages in a place that belonged to no city.

steps.title: רבי יהודה בן בבא sends his students away and is killed
steps.stepSummary: When the enemy found them, רבי יהודה בן בבא told his students to run, said he could not escape anyway, and was killed with three hundred iron spears.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the enemies found them, he said to them: 'My sons, run!' They said to him: 'רבי, and what will happen to you?' He said to them: 'I am lying before them like a stone that no one can turn over.' People said: the soldiers did not leave until they stuck three hundred iron spears into his body and made his body like a sieve.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the story: רבי יהודה בן בבא gave up his life so his newly ordained students could escape.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because he was old and could not run, he knew trying to save him would only get everyone killed. His death protected the students, and through them the chain of סמיכה. This shows that ordained judges, who could judge דיני קנסות, existed long after the סנהדרין left, so the challenge from Step 23 against רבי יצחק בר אבדימי still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: like a stone no one bothers to turn over, meaning he could not be moved or saved

steps.whatToRemember: The story proves that ordained judges kept judging דיני קנסות well after the חורבן, so the claim that קנסות stopped when the סנהדרין moved cannot be right as stated.

phrases.english: When the enemies discovered them,
he said to them: My sons, run!

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: רַבִּי, וְאַתָּה מָה תְּהֵא עָלֶיךָ?
phrases.english: They said to him: Our teacher, and what will become of you?
He said to them: I am lying before them
like a stone that cannot be overturned.
phrases.notes: He means he is too old and weak to get away, so they should save themselves.

phrases.english: They said: they did not move from there
until they stuck into his body
three hundred iron spears,
and made his body like a sieve.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן שֶׁהִכִּירוּ בָּהֶם אוֹיְבִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the story begun in Step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה בן בבא was martyred to protect his ordained students and keep סמיכה alive.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: after the סנהדרין moved, capital cases stopped, not fines
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק fixes רבי יצחק בר אבדימי's statement: forty years before the חורבן they stopped judging דיני נפשות, not דיני קנסות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Do not say 'cases of fines.' Rather, say that they stopped judging capital cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 23 by changing the wording of רבי יצחק בר אבדימי's statement from Step 22.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story showed that דיני קנסות were still judged long after the חורבן, so they could not have stopped when the סנהדרין moved. What did stop then was דיני נפשות, capital cases. That fits both the dates from Step 20 and the story of רבי יהודה בן בבא.

keyTerms.meaning: do not say (the wording should be changed)
capital cases, cases where the punishment is death

steps.whatToRemember: Final answer: the סנהדרין moving forty years before the חורבן ended דיני נפשות. דיני קנסות continued as long as there were judges with סמיכה, which רבי יהודה בן בבא made sure of.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of cases: קנסות (fines) need ordained judges, while נפשות (capital cases) also need the סנהדרין sitting in its proper place. That is why one stopped earlier than the other.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
Do not say cases of fines,
phrases.notes: He is changing the wording of רבי יצחק בר אבדימי's statement from Step 22.

phrases.english: rather, that they no longer judged capital cases.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תֵּימָא דִּינֵי קְנָסוֹת, אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא דָּנוּ דִּינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the main challenge in Step 23 and resolves it, now that the story has shown fines were still judged.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the wording of an earlier statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יצחק בר אבדימי's statement as quoted said that fines stopped when the סנהדרין moved, which goes against the story of רבי יהודה בן בבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The correct wording is that capital cases stopped when the סנהדרין moved; fines continued.

steps.title: Why did they stop judging capital cases?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the סנהדרין stopped judging דיני נפשות forty years before the חורבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the judges stopped hearing death-penalty cases, as רב נחמן בר יצחק just said. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 28 told us what happened: דיני נפשות stopped. Now the גמרא wants the reason, since judges would not just walk away from a מצוה for no cause.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: He means: why did they stop judging death-penalty cases, as we just learned in step 28?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind רב נחמן בר יצחק's corrected statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the סנהדרין stopped judging דיני נפשות forty years before the חורבן.

steps.title: Too many murderers, so they moved away
steps.stepSummary: There were so many murderers that the court could not judge them all, so the judges chose to leave their place so that no one would be found guilty of a death-penalty crime.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once they saw that there were so many murderers and they could not judge them, they said: It is better that we move from place to place, so that people will not be sentenced to death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: murder became so common that the court could not keep up, so the סנהדרין left its proper place on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving their place was a deliberate choice, not a punishment from outside. Once the סנהדרין was not in its place, no court could give a death sentence. That way people would not be declared liable to die at a time when the courts could not properly carry it out.

keyTerms.meaning: We will be exiled / move away
They will be found liable (here, to death)

steps.confusionAlert: The judges did not stop judging all cases. They left their proper place so that only death-penalty cases could no longer be judged.

phrases.english: Once they saw that murderers had become numerous
and they were not able to judge them,
they said: It is better that we be exiled from place to place,
so that they will not be found liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דַּחֲזוֹ דִּנְפִישִׁי לְהוּ רוֹצְחִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Murderers became so many that the court could not judge them, so the סנהדרין left its place on purpose, which stopped all death sentences.

steps.title: A פסוק shows the place makes the judging possible
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says judgment comes 'from that place', which teaches that the place of the סנהדרין is what allows death-penalty cases to be judged.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And you shall do according to the word that they tell you from that place.' This teaches that the place is what makes it work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק to explain why leaving their place stopped the death penalty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'from that place' show that the judging depends on the סנהדרין sitting in its proper place. So once the סנהדרין left, no court anywhere could judge דיני נפשות. That is why moving away worked.

keyTerms.meaning: The place causes it (the place is what makes it happen)

steps.whatToRemember: The סנהדרין left its place on purpose because of the many murderers, and since the פסוק ties judgment to 'that place', leaving it ended all death-penalty cases.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And you shall do according to the word'

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר יַגִּידוּ לְךָ מִן הַמָּקוֹם הַהוּא״,
phrases.english: 'that they will tell you from that place,'
this teaches that the place causes it.
phrases.notes: In other words, death-penalty cases can only be judged while the סנהדרין sits in its proper place.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: וְעָשִׂיתָ עַל פִּי הַדָּבָר אֲשֶׁר יַגִּידוּ לְךָ מִן הַמָּקוֹם הַהוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for why leaving their place stopped death-penalty cases.
steps.raayaObject: That leaving the proper place ends all דיני נפשות.

steps.title: Only 180 years of Roman rule? A teaching seems to say more
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the earlier statement that Rome ruled 180 years before the חורבן and starts to challenge it with a teaching of רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: One hundred and eighty years, and no more? But רבי יוסי the great taught:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the earlier count of 180 years of Roman rule and asks if it was really only that long. It is setting up a challenge; the teaching itself comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא said, in the name of רבי יוסי, that Rome ruled over Israel for 180 years before the חורבן. Now it brings a teaching that seems to give a longer time. The quote of the teaching continues in the next part of the text.

phrases.english: One hundred and eighty years, and no more?
But didn't רבי יוסי the great teach:
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוסי בן חלפתא himself, the same one the 180 years was said in the name of. His teaching continues next.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵאָה וּשְׁמֹנִים, וְתוּ לָא? וְהָתָנֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of the סנהדרין and returns to the earlier statement about 180 years of Roman rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier statement that Rome ruled over Israel for 180 years before the חורבן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A teaching of רבי יוסי seems to give a longer period of Roman rule, which would contradict the 180-year count.
